speaker: Doctor
text: I notice your newborn has increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. Can you tell me exactly when you first noticed this jaundice, and was it present within the first 24 hours of life?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-week-old female newborn. The patient has been experiencing increasing yellow discoloration of her eyes and skin for 2 days. She was born at 39 weeks' gestation, initially weighed 3066 g and now weighs 3200 g. The patient is exclusively breastfed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Are the baby's stools pale or clay-colored, and is her urine dark or concentrated?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Total Bilirubin: 16.1 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin: 0.7 mg/dL, Indirect Bilirubin: 15.4 mg/dL

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show predominantly indirect hyperbilirubinemia, which is common in breastfed infants, but I need to rule out other causes. Has the baby had any episodes of poor feeding, lethargy, or high-pitched crying, and are her stools consistently yellow/brown?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Increasing yellow discoloration of the eyes and skin. I also have Exclusively breastfed, Brother died 3 months after liver surgery.

speaker: Doctor
text: The family history of your brother's early death after liver surgery is highly concerning for a metabolic disorder like Galactosemia. I need to check her blood sugar and metabolic profile immediately. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Glucose, Urine_Reducing_Substances, Galactose_1_Phosphate_Uridyltransferase

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal galactosemia screen and the family history of early liver failure, I need to rule out Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Deficiency as a cause of neonatal cholestasis. REQUEST TEST: Alpha_1_Antitrypsin_Level, Liver_Function_Tests

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Alpha-1 Antitrypsin Level: NORMAL READINGS, Liver_Function_Tests: Bilirubin_Total: 16.1 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.7 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 22 U/L, AST: 12 U/L, ALT: 12 U/L

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal liver enzymes and direct bilirubin rule out cholestasis, confirming this is unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia. Given the family history, I must check for hemolysis, so REQUEST TEST: Blood_Typing_and_Coombs_Test, Peripheral_Smear.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Typing and Coombs Test: Baby Blood Type O Negative, Mother Blood Type O Negative, Direct Coombs Test Negative. Peripheral Smear: Normal red blood cell morphology, no schistocytes or spherocytes observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since hemolytic causes are ruled out, I suspect a metabolic issue affecting bilirubin conjugation. REQUEST TEST: G6PD_Enzyme_Activity

speaker: Doctor
text: With hemolysis and other metabolic disorders ruled out, this presentation of late-onset unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia in an exclusively breastfed infant is classic for breast milk jaundice. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast Milk Jaundice
